# Splitting Criteria and Prioritization

Also called: Splitting Metrics, Densification Prioritization

## Overview
Splitting Criteria and Prioritization determines which Gaussian primitives in a 3D Gaussian Splatting scene should undergo densification (splitting or cloning) based on their contribution to reconstruction error or complexity. It solves the problem of inefficient primitive allocation by ensuring that new Gaussians are spawned only where necessary, preventing uniform distribution in simple regions and insufficient coverage in complex areas. It sets itself apart from sibling methods by defining the specific scalar metric used to rank Gaussians for densification, ranging from multi-view gradient aggregation to complexity-aware importance scores.

## Shared principles
The family shares the goal of optimizing the trade-off between rendering quality and computational cost by dynamically adjusting the number of Gaussians. All methods operate during the training phase, evaluating a scalar metric per Gaussian to decide if it exceeds a threshold defined in [Adaptive Density Control](9188-adaptive-density-control.md). The core mechanism involves computing a value that represents either the local reconstruction error, the spatial complexity, or the gradient magnitude, and using this value to prioritize which primitives are candidates for splitting or cloning.

## Subtopics

### [Multi-View Density Control Criterion](5663-multi-view-density-control-criterion.md)
The Multi-View Density Control Criterion is a densification strategy designed to resolve invalid vector arithmetic when applying standard Adaptive Density Control to multi-view training pipelines. Standard ADC sums 2D positional gradients from multiple viewpoints, which is mathematically invalid because these vectors reside in different image planes. This criterion replaces vector addition with the summation of squared norms, ensuring that error metrics remain valid across multiple views. It sets itself apart from siblings by focusing specifically on the geometric consistency of gradient aggregation in multi-view settings. See [Multi-View Density Control Criterion](5663-multi-view-density-control-criterion.md).

### [Complexity-Aware Adaptive Density Control](16126-complexity-aware-adaptive-density-control.md)
Complexity-Aware Adaptive Density Control replaces opacity-only heuristics with a composite metric combining opacity, spatial scale, and local image complexity. It solves the problem of inefficient primitive allocation by biasing densification and pruning toward regions with high reconstruction error while preserving large primitives in simple regions to maintain uniform degradation across different levels of detail. It differs from siblings by explicitly modeling the spatial footprint of primitives via scale and using a complexity field to modulate the importance score. See [Complexity-Aware Adaptive Density Control](16126-complexity-aware-adaptive-density-control.md).

### Distortion-based Gaussian Splitting Prioritization
A criterion for prioritizing which Gaussians to split, based on rate-distortion optimization to maximize PSNR gain. It associates a reconstruction Squared Error $SE_{c,i}$ to each Gaussian, defined as the sum of weighted squared differences between the rendered image $R^{(c)}(p)$ and the ground-truth image $I^{(c)}(p)$ for pixels $p$ covered by the Gaussian in camera view $c$ [S1]. The Gaussians with the highest $SE_{c,i}$ are prioritized for splitting to reduce local reconstruction error [S1].

## Background
The concept of prioritizing densification based on error metrics originates from rate-distortion optimization principles in computer graphics. Early work by [17] (cited in [S1]) used a splitting mechanism that did not account for opacity variations, while the proposed distortion-based criterion spreads the error metric across Gaussians to guide densification effectively [S1]. This approach aims to maximize PSNR gain by splitting Gaussians that induce the highest reconstruction error.
